tldr: PaperQA is a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) agent that dynamically searches, gathers evidence, and answers questions over full-text scientific literature, outperforming existing LLMs and matching human experts on scientific QA benchmarks.
contributions: PaperQA, an agent-based RAG system for scientific question answering with modular search, evidence gathering, and answer generation tools
LitQA, a new benchmark of 50 multiple-choice questions from biomedical literature published after September 2021, requiring retrieval and synthesis from full-text papers
Demonstration that PaperQA outperforms existing LLMs and commercial tools and matches human expert performance
methods: PaperQA is an agent built on LangChain using four LLM instances (GPT-4 as agent, answer, and ask LLM; GPT-3.5 as summary LLM) with three tools: search (queries Google Scholar for top-5 accessible papers, chunks text into 4,000-character pieces embedded with text-embedding-ada-002), gather evidence (retrieves relevant chunks via vector search with max marginal relevance and scores them 1-10 via a summary LLM), and answer question (uses a priori prompting via ask LLM then generates a cited answer). The agent iteratively searches and gathers evidence until at least five pieces of evidence are collected from multiple sources.
results: PaperQA scored 86.3% on PubMedQA blind compared to GPT-4's 57.9% (30-point improvement). On LitQA, PaperQA outperformed all tested models and commercial tools and was comparable to human experts in both performance and time (~2.4 hours vs. humans' 2.5 hours), at a cost of $0.18 per question (~$3.75/hour). PaperQA produced zero hallucinated citations, while GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Claude-2 all hallucinated citations at notable rates. PaperQA also exhibited better uncertainty calibration, answering incorrectly at a lower rate than competing tools.
limitations: PDF parsing errors and search engine/API failure rates exist
PaperQA may cite secondary sources mentioned in primary sources it cannot directly access, potentially leading to hallucination
Some LitQA questions may still be partially answerable via latent pre-training knowledge, as GPT-4 and Claude-2 performed above random despite post-cutoff questions
Standard QA benchmarks (MedQA, MMLU, etc.) test commonly known facts not typically found in academic papers, which PaperQA may not perform as well on
